results.content:
5.0

Based on 19 reviews

Review Context.dev?

Reviewers describe Context.dev as a fast, reliable web-fetch and enrichment layer that is simple to integrate and especially useful for AI agents. Users say it turns web data into cleaner, more usable output for meeting prep and other agent workflows. Makers of OpenSEO and Migma AI say it handles JavaScript-heavy sites well, performs better than alternatives for speed and result quality, and avoids extra scraper, proxy, and cleanup work. Main criticisms are limited: docs could use more examples, brand color extraction needs refinement, and compliance visibility around site policy changes is unclear.

#### What's great

I have been super happy with Context.dev its not a perfect product by all means but the top tier support and usually 1-2day turnaround time on requests is pushing it close to being perfect!

#### What needs improvement

For me right now its mostly brand color extraction being a bit more polished and better at detecting whats primary and what is an accent color.

#### vs Alternatives

FirecrawlFirecrawl

I never liked the concurrent browser limit of Firecrawl but thought this was just the industry standard until I used Context.dev which does not enforce such a limit. Especially in AI apps where you have lots of concurrency thats a no brainer. [...] Report

#### What's great

Been using it as the web-fetch layer for a coding agent setup instead of maintaining my own scraper/proxy stack. The markdown-cleanup output is genuinely good for feeding pages into an LLM without a bunch of nav/footer junk eating tokens, and the brand/company enrichment endpoints saved me from writing a bunch of one-off logo/favicon scraping code. Typed SDK meant it was a 10 minute integration like they claim, not a "10 minutes then 2 hours of debugging" situation.
